sentenceSets.sentence: The heirloom she had expected to be valuable turned out to be little more than a Victorian bauble.

answerChoices.reasoning: Bauble and trinket are nearly synonymous—both mean inexpensive decorative objects—though trinket may emphasize crafted novelty more.
Both describe small decorative items of little value, but knickknack emphasizes small ornamental objects, while bauble emphasizes glittering ornamentation.
Both describe small objects kept for decoration, but curio emphasizes objects of interest or rarity, while bauble emphasizes glittering trinkets.
Both describe decorative objects, but ornament is broader and can be valuable, while bauble specifically means an inexpensive trinket.
The object is a small decorative item, but toy emphasizes something for play or amusement, not necessarily decorative.
A bauble is novel and decorative, but novelty emphasizes newness or unusual quality more than the nature of the object.
Both describe showy objects of little value, but gewgaw may emphasize showiness more, while bauble emphasizes glittering nature.
A bauble may be a souvenir, but souvenir emphasizes a remembrance of a place, not necessarily cheap or glittering.
The heirloom turned out to be a bauble, not a treasure; treasure describes something of great value.
The heirloom was merely a bauble; heirloom implies something valuable passed through generations.
The object is a bauble of little value; masterpiece describes something of exceptional quality.

sentenceSets.sentence: The museum's gift shop was filled with cheap baubles—plastic figurines, painted shells, and glittering costume jewelry—all labeled as authentic souvenirs.

answerChoices.reasoning: Both describe items of little genuine value, but fakes emphasize fraudulent copies, while baubles simply mean cheap trinkets.
Both describe copies of original items, but replicas are often acknowledging copies, while baubles are cheap items regardless of authenticity.
Both describe non-authentic items, but imitations emphasize copying, while baubles emphasize cheapness and showiness.
Both describe items for sale, but merchandise is broader, while baubles specifically mean cheap trinkets.
The gift shop items are cheap, but junk emphasizes worthlessness or garbage, while baubles emphasize decorative cheapness.
The items are novel and decorative, but novelties emphasize newness or unusual quality more than cheapness.
The items are handmade or crafted, but craft emphasizes construction technique, not cheapness.
The items may be collected, but collectibles emphasizes value for collectors, while baubles mean cheap trinkets.
The gift shop sells cheap baubles; treasures describe valuable items.
The items are cheap baubles; investments describe items of lasting value.
The items labeled as authentic are merely baubles; artifacts are genuine objects of historical or scientific value.

sentenceSets.sentence: The magician drew the audience's attention to a glittering bauble while secretly palming the card necessary for the trick.

answerChoices.reasoning: The bauble is used as a distraction, but distraction describes the effect, while bauble describes the object used.
Both are misdirection tactics in magic, but sleight refers to a skilled hand movement, while bauble refers to the object used for misdirection.
The bauble serves as a decoy, but decoy describes something used for misdirection, while bauble describes the specific object.
The bauble creates an illusion, but illusion refers to the false perception created, while bauble is the object used.
The bauble is a prop, but prop is broader and includes all objects used in performance, not specifically decorative.
The bauble is a device for misdirection, but device refers to any mechanism, not necessarily decorative.
The bauble is used as a feint, but feint refers to a deceptive move, not the object itself.
The bauble is part of a ruse, but ruse refers to the deceptive strategy, not the object.
The magician palms a card while drawing attention to the bauble; they are different objects.
The bauble distracts from the reveal; reveal describes showing something to the audience.
The bauble prevents exposure of the trick; exposure means revealing the secret.
